correctness.rationale: The Euler factor for \((-1)^{\omega(n)}\) is \((1-2p^{-s})/(1-p^{-s})\). Factoring out \(p=2\) and one reciprocal zeta function gives the displayed analytic product. The residual odd-prime product converges normally near \(s=1\) and its logarithmic derivative is \(S\). Expansion of the prime-2 factor, zeta reciprocal and residual product gives the exact cubic coefficient. The strict sign follows from an integral upper bound on every remaining prime and rational exponential checks for the first seven primes: \(S<2.092239<13/6<\gamma+(5/2)\log2\). The standalone checker reproduces the rational inequalities; finite examples are not used as proof of an infinite claim.
